subject: Commit shift and voucher payment model proposal for Q4 top-up
messages:
From: Sam Weller <sam.weller@acumentech.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acumentech.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mid-contract capacity increase — options and discount asks

Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We need to add capacity to support a pilot across two additional product teams starting next month. Our procurement team is asking whether we can avoid a full contract amendment (legal turnaround is slow on our side) and instead do a one-off top-up with some kind of pre-paid credit voucher or invoice-backed credit.

Key asks from Acumen:
- Add ~18M tokens/month for 6 months (pilot) with ability to convert to an ongoing commit if successful.
- Discounting: procurement is asking for a single-digit to low-teens discount vs list for the top-up (they suggested 10%).
- Co-term: if we convert to a committed contract, we want co-terming options and pro-rata alignment to our Jun renewal.

Can you outline the models you can support (prepaid voucher, short-term commit, or pro-rate add-on) and expected pricing / lead times? Also need a statement of work (SOW) for usage and billing treatment for our finance team.

Best,
Sam
Procurement Lead | AcumenTech

---

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Weller <sam.weller@acumentech.com>
Cc: procurement@acumentech.com, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:35:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Mid-contract capacity increase — options and discount asks

Sam — really appreciate the clear bullets. We can support a few practical paths that avoid a long legal amendment and keep you running while you evaluate converting to committed capacity. High level (summary attached): Voucher (prepaid credit) model, Short-term committed top-up (6-month term), or One-time invoice + pro-rata conversion.

Attached: Voucher_Model_Proposal_v1.pdf (walks through economics), SOW_AcumenTech_topup.xlsx (billing and usage mapping), redwood_pricing_sheet.csv (list prices + sample discounts).

Quick bullets:
- Voucher (recommended for speed): You pre-pay for token credits upfront. Credits redeem at a slightly discounted rate vs list. No contract amendment required; we issue a simplified purchase order receipt and apply credits automatically. Good for pilots.
  - Example: pre-pay for 100M tokens. List $0.0008/token => $80k; voucher rate with a 10% uplift discount = $0.00072/token => $72k.
  - Voucher expires after 12 months; ability to convert leftover credits to committed capacity at time of conversion with partial credit applied.
- 6-month short commit: We can do a temporary committed bucket with a 6-month term and a capped discount (we can flex up to 12% depending on total committed run-rate). Includes billing as a reserved capacity SKU — faster internal chargeback for your finance team.
- Invoice + pro-rate: One-off invoice for a consumption estimate, with clear pro-rata conversion rules if you convert to a long-term commit.

Trade-offs: voucher is fastest and lowest-ops but has less favorable GAAP treatment for some customers; committed top-up gives better unit economics but requires a short term commercial addendum.

Next steps I suggest: 1) You confirm which lane (voucher vs 6-mo commit), 2) procurement approves PO or we prepare an expedited amendment, 3) we provision capacity (24–72 hours for voucher, 3–5 business days for committed top-up).

If helpful, I can propose a capped discount table (5/8/12%) tied to contract length and volume — pinged Neha to confirm approval band.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity increase — options and discount asks

Looping in Monica for commercial ops and legal triage. Aditya — voucher sounds fine for a pilot, but we should set a maximum discount cap and clear conversion rules. Proposed guardrails:
- Voucher cap: up to 12% off list for pre-pay vouchers <= $150k; above $150k needs AM approval.
- Conversion credit: unused voucher balance converts to committed capacity at the higher of the voucher rate or 85% of the then-current committed rate (prevents large arbitrage).
- No change to SLAs; any committed conversion carries normal SLA/uptime terms.

Monica — can you prepare a one-page amendment template + quick SOW that procurement can sign or attach to the PO? Prefer PDF that procurement can attach to their PO.

Neha
Head of Commercial Solutions | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Sam — attaching the SOW and a short amendment stub you can attach to a PO. I also created a simplified invoice template if you want to route this through procurement as a one-off charge.

Attachment stubs included: SOW_AcumenTech_topup.xlsx (usage mapping + billing terms), Voucher_Model_Proposal_v1.pdf (economics), redwood_pricing_sheet.csv

Key commercial summary for procurement:
- Option A (Voucher): Pre-pay credits, voucher rate = list less 10% (example tier). Voucher valid 12 months. No legal amendment; attach one-page SOW to PO.
- Option B (6-month short commit): 8–12% discount depending on volume. Requires short addendum executed electronically.
- Billing: Voucher invoiced up front; short-commit invoiced monthly as reserved capacity.

Please review and let us know which option procurement prefers. If you select Option A, we will send a DocuSign-ready invoice + voucher agreement for signature; once PO arrives we provision within 24 hours.

Best,
Monica Patel
